Last week, Apple reported that iPad revenue for the quarter ending in June fell 5% year-over-year. Now, a new report puts this decline into context with the overall tablet market performance in the second quarter of 2026. Here are the details.

Global tablet shipments decline

According to a new report from research firm Omdia (cited by MacMagazine), global tablet shipments in the second quarter of 2026 fell to 35.5 million units, a year-over-year decline of 9.9%.

The report notes that although Apple's shipments fell 7.5%, it still held a firm grip on market leadership, shipping a total of 13.5 million iPads for a market share of 37.8%. Samsung ranked second with 5.8 million units shipped and a 16.3% share, followed by Lenovo (11.1%), Xiaomi (8%), and Huawei (7.7%).

Among the top five vendors, Lenovo was the only one to record growth, with shipments surging 27.1% compared to the second quarter of 2025.

Omdia pointed out that vendors outside the top five collectively accounted for 19.1% of total shipments, but their combined shipments fell 23.5% year-over-year.

Below is Omdia research manager Himani Mukka's response to this report:

Mukka added that, facing ongoing component supply constraints, "vendors will largely not prioritise the tablet category." They expect to "concentrate limited resources on flagship and high-end models, further tilting the product mix toward premium devices."
